cases.description: Pete exits long TLRY stock at $12.06 for $.20 loss — Exit+Long badges, explicit exit price

input.rawHtml: Exit Long TLRY $12.06 for $.20 loss. No staying power. I was looking for $.20 on the upside and follow thru. Did not get it and this is not a stock I would want to hold overnight
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: Clean long stock exit: Exit+Long badges, ticker, exit price ($12.06), P&L ('$.20 loss'). Exit badge = CLOSE action. Long badge = was long stock, now closing. orderType=STOCK, direction=LONG on the open position.

cases.description: Pete exits short MRVL stock at $85.12 for $.40 gain — Exit+Short badges, brief message

input.rawHtml: Exit Short MRVL $85.12 for $.40 gain.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: Short stock exit: Exit+Short badges. Critical badge semantics: Short badge on an EXIT message = closing a SHORT stock position (buy-to-cover), NOT a new short sale. The position direction is SHORT (was selling shares); the exit action covers it. orderType=STOCK must be preserved.

cases.description: Pete exits short ORLY stock at $94.11 for $.20 gain — Exit+Short badges, trader commentary

input.rawHtml: Exit Short ORLY $94.11 for $.20 gain. The stock looks like a good short, but it has not been moving down with the market like I would like to see. Getting late in the day so taking the gain.
input.author: Pete

cases.notes: Short stock exit with trader reasoning. 'The stock looks like a good short' is bearish market commentary — it does NOT mean a new short entry. The Exit badge is authoritative: this is a CLOSE of an existing SHORT position. LLM must not mistake the reasoning text for a new signal.

cases.description: Hariseldon exits NVDA stock with $2.15 profit per share — Exit badge only (no Long/Short), profit-per-share format

input.rawHtml: Exit NVDA with $2.15 profit per share (1,000)
input.author: Hariseldon

cases.notes: Hariseldon style: Exit badge only (no Long/Short direction badge). Profit expressed as '$X per share (quantity)' rather than a percentage or exit price. The '(1,000)' is share count context, not a price. Must still resolve to a CLOSE of the NVDA STOCK position. orderType=STOCK, hasTradeId=true.
